jobs.occupation: Accessing orbitronics and twistronics with microscopic and ultrafast angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Physics and Astronomy programme. The position is available from February 2027 or later.

Research area and project description:

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Aarhus University, invites applications for a PhD position, starting February 1st, 2027, offering applicants an exciting opportunity to join a new research project on orbitronics and metastable states in two-dimensional quantum materials.

The project involves fabrication of devices and their integration with the existing angle-resolved photoemission (ARPES) infrastructure at the ASTRID2 light source to discover quantum geometric effects and their link to new forms of transport phenomena.

The aim of the project is to develop new types of 2D material devices that can realize orbital, spin and valley Hall effects that form the basis for prototypical memory devices. A series of novel infrastructures will be applied to achieve these goals, including semi-automated fabrication systems in inert environments, clean-room facilities for device production, micro-focused synchrotron light for ARPES characterization at ASTRID2 as well as ultrafast femtosecond laser pulses for optical control of the materials.

The major activities include:

• Design and manufacturing of advanced 2D devices that are compatible with the microARPES experiment at ASTRID2 with the specific aim to uncover orbital-driven phenomena in materials.

• Combining synchrotron and ultrafast laser sources to visualize, excite and control electronic states with distinct orbital and spin textures in quantum materials.

• Isolation, twisting and stacking of monolayer metallic and semiconducting transition metal dichalcogenide, including materials that are sensitive to ambient conditions.

• Development of new techniques to isolate and integrate such air-sensitive materials with devices for photoemission experiments carried out in UHV conditions.

• Applying a state-of-the-art laser beamline integrated with the ASTRID2 synchrotron light source for femtosecond control of electronic structure of 2D materials.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. When - as here - you apply for a specific project, please simply copy the project description above, and upload it as a PDF in the application. If you wish to, you can indicate an URL where further information can be found.

Qualifications and specific competences:

Applicants should hold or be about to obtain a Master’s degree in Physics, Nanoscience or similar and with a keen interest in Condensed Matter Physics (or related field).

The applicant is expected to be a team-player that is strongly motivated to work with students, scientists, engineers and external collaborators as well as being supportive and open towards other group members.

The applicant should be highly motivated towards building expertise in relation to ultra-high vacuum experiments, synchrotron and laser beamlines as well as 2D material fabrication.

jobs.occupation: Quantum Control of Emission in Valleytronic Materials
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Physics and Astronomy programme. The position is available from February 2027 or later.

Research area and project description:

We are seeking a candidate for a fully funded 3-year PhD project at the Department of Physics and Astronomy, Aarhus University, in the new group of Asst. Prof. Christian Frydendahl, as part of a DFF Sapere Aude research grant.

Compact, integrable sources of circularly polarized light (CPL) are a key enabling technology for chip-scale quantum technologies, but electrically driven sources of pure CPL do not yet exist. Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) emit left- or right-handed CPL depending on which band structure valley, K or K', an electron-hole pair recombines in. Ordinarily, this occurs with an equal 50/50 split between the two valleys.

This project aims to build a new light-emitting diode geometry in which the Valley Hall effect, another intrinsic property of these materials, filters the valley index of the charge carriers during transport, enabling a purely electrically pumped source of CPL. Inducing valley polarization electrically rather than optically is one of the key open challenges in the emerging field of device-based valleytronics.

The project also includes a planned 6-month external research stay at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), where you will develop and fabricate nanophotonic cavities for integration with the new diode design, enhancing its emission and CPL purity further via the Purcell effect.

Your general working tasks would be:

• van der Waals stacking of hBN-encapsulated TMDC monolayers

• Nanofabrication in the AU/SUTD cleanroom facilities (EBL, RIE, metal deposition)

• Opto-electronic characterization: probe station, polarization- and time-resolved spectroscopy at room- and cryogenic temperatures

• Publishing results and presenting at international conferences

• Participating in general dissemination and teaching activities

We are looking for a hands-on experimentalist who works well independently and as a part of a team. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English are a requirement.

As Teledyne RESON’s new Toolmaker, you will be part of the Technology and Products department. The group cooperates in defining, developing, testing, prepare production setup and handover of new products to Operations for numerous product lines.

Our products consist of real-time Single- and Multi-beam Sonar Systems, Inertial Navigation System and related products. The product lines span from small low power products for autonomous vehicle drones (ASV/AUV) to high-end deepwater sonar systems for large research vessels.

You will be working in the mechanical team with focus be on transducer prototyping, manufacturing processes, automation, and production support for new and existing products. You will be part of development projects with design for manufacturability reviews, production tooling, procurement and set to work of production machines, prototyping build and documentation.

• Prototype assembly of small- and full-scale acoustic sensors working close with the transducer designer

• Material knowledge with metal, glue, plastic and urethane materials

• Support and maintenance of production equipment.

• Support to the daily operational tasks incl. troubleshooting and NCR/MRB-handling

• Corrective And Preventive Action (CAPA)

• Production documentation support to assembly- and test procedures

Job Requirements:

• Experience with setup and operation of lathes, milling machines, grinding machines, and jig grinders

• Experience with CAD software is preferred.

• You are structured, systematic and quality-minded

• Drive and ability to complete task to agreed deadline

• Enjoy working both independently and in teams

• Proactive, positive and supporting personality

Educational level:

You have an education as a Toolmaker, Machinist, or other background as a skilled operator of machine tools.

Fluent in English to a professional level

HEGSØ Search & Consulting, chief consultant Anders Hegelskov, Phone: +45 3035 6405 – Mail: ah@hegsoe.dk

_Do you want to help build one coherent way for a global technology organization to deliver, bringing scaled product-centric ways of working project and program execution _ together into a single system, rather than running them as separate worlds? Are you as comfortable helping shape that system and turning it into ways of working people actually use in the room with the people who'll actually use it?

We are hiring a Manager, Delivery Enablement to help shape and evolve how Pandora's D&T organization delivers. D&T spans the full range of technology that keeps Pandora running: from customer-facing platforms to manufacturing systems, ERP, logistics and operations, security, covering build, run, and operate across all of it. This role does not carry people-management responsibility. Your impact comes through the quality of what you build and how well it lands across the organization.

You'll join Delivery Enablement, a team combining operating-model design and implementation, coaching, and delivery tooling capability. It's built to make Digital & Technology (D&T) faster, clearer, and more coherent at scale. Delivery Enablement sits within Delivery Excellence, alongside the Scrum Masters, Delivery Leads, and Project and Program Managers. You will work with the wider team to shape ideas and turn them into practical ways of working across D&T.

Your Role

You will help harmonize and evolve how scaled agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery work together, building on what already exists across D&T rather than replacing it, closing gaps only where they cause real friction. This is as much about leading change as it is about designing structure. You will also advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape, and help teams and entities build the capability to adopt the model as it evolves.

You will work closely with the wider delivery community, as well as product, engineering, and leadership more broadly, to facilitate structural workshops, build the case for change, and make sure what gets designed is something people actually want to use, not just a document on a shelf. A key part of the role is building the relationships, networks and momentum needed to bring ideas to life across D&T.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Co-design and evolve how scaled agile and structured, plan-driven delivery work together, harmonizing and building on existing practice rather than replacing it

• Advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape

• Lead workstreams that take new or improved delivery processes (for example dependency management or capacity planning) from idea through pilot, rollout, adoption and continuous improvement

• Support onboarding and capability-building for teams and entities adopting the model, working alongside the team's wider coaching capability

• Facilitate structural workshops and working sessions with the wider delivery community to shape and pressure-test the model

• Build relationships, networks and communities that help change spread and stick across D&T

• Pilot approaches, learn from feedback, and scale what works

• Help translate high-level decisions about how delivery is prioritized, funded, resourced, and executed into practical structures and standards teams can use

• Help projects and programs connect into the wider D&T Operating Model, including common governance, planning, dependency management and delivery tooling

• Contribute to keeping the model coherent as it evolves, spotting where new structures overlap or conflict with what already exists

• Provide point-in-time advisory support where operating-model gaps are most costly

• Document how the operating model works and how it evolves over time

• Build strong relationships across the wider delivery community and leadership to ensure what gets built is genuinely adopted

What Is Needed to Succeed

• ignificant experience in delivery transformation, operating-model implementation, PMO, program/project delivery or organizational change within a large, complex technology organization

• Demonstrated experience working across both scaled/product-centric agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery, with enough understanding to contribute credibly to how they work together

• Track record of taking new ways of working from idea through implementation, adoption and continuous improvement

• Ideally a mix of hands-on delivery experience and consulting or advisory experience, but real, first-hand delivery experience matters more than advisory polish alone

• Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, and narrative-building skills across senior and operational levels

• Comfortable leading through organizational change: helping people, not just structures, adapt as delivery models shift

• Able to build trust, networks and momentum without relying on formal authority

• Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate your own analysis, design, and documentation work

• Working understanding of how delivery tooling (e.g. Jira/Confluence, or equivalent) underpins an operating model, enough to design frameworks that translate into practice, not to configure the tooling yourself

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity: building on foundations already in motion, while still shaping significant parts of the model from scratch

• Systems thinking: able to see cross-domain and cross-entity dependencies, not just local fixes

• Pragmatic bias toward incremental, adoptable change over comprehensive upfront design

• Relevant certifications (e.g. PMP, PRINCE2, SAFe) are an advantage

Did we get your attention?

We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (AIAS) is pleased to announce an exclusive fellowship opportunity for a researcher who holds a position at a Swedish research institution. The fellowship is made possible through a collaboration with Riksbankens Jubileumsfond in Sweden.The purpose of the AIAS-RJ fellowship is to strengthen the ties and expand collaborations between the Swedish and Danish research communities.

Why apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

AIAS is a haven for intellectual exploration, hosting excellent researchers eager to develop their work in an interdisciplinary, international and collaborative environment. AIAS nurtures an innovative atmosphere where breakthroughs emerge through transparent, inclusive and reflective discussions, offering a space for engagement and creativity.

The AIAS-RJ fellowship gives the selected fellow the opportunity to concentrate on their own research interests while also being an active member of the AIAS research community and participating in and contributing to seminars and activities beyond their own field of expertise. The fellow must be eager to engage in the interdisciplinary community at AIAS and expand research collaborations with colleagues at Aarhus University.

Who can apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

The call is open to curiosity-driven researchers who:

• are of any nationality who hold a tenured position at a Swedish research institution

• work within the humanities and social sciences

• have a research experience of minimum 4 years after completion of the PhD

A unique interdisciplinary platform at AIAS

AIAS fosters connections, sparks ideas and dissolves boundaries as fellows engage with researchers from different disciplines within the Institute and across departments and research hubs at Aarhus University. Therefore, the call welcomes applications from all research areas and themes.

With a location within the unique campus of Aarhus University, AIAS functions as an interdisciplinary platform that connects researchers across Aarhus University and international scholars. AIAS has fellows who work in thematic groups or in individual fellowships, and hosts events and activities, which AIAS-RJ fellows are welcome to join and contribute to.

AIAS and Aarhus University strive to create a multidisciplinary, inclusive academic environment and to be an inspiring workplace for all by fostering a culture in which the individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The fellowship includes

The AIAS-RJ Fellow is offered:

• a salary based on seniority (employment conditions and wages are regulated through the Danish collective union agreements)

• travel costs to and from Aarhus

• relocation assistance

• a moderate budget for research-related costs

The AIAS-RJ Fellow will have office space at AIAS and can participate in academic training activities, conferences and workshops at AIAS. They will also be affiliated with the relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

How to apply: Application process and deadline

Applications must be submitted online via the system: GrantOne.

In the ‘Guide for Applicants,’ you can find the detailed application requirements and more information on the structure of the application system, the selection criteria and the selection process.

Timeline of the application process

• Opening of call: August 2026.

• Deadline for applications: 24 November 2026 at 12.00 (noon) CET.

• Evaluation and selection period: December 2026 - March 2027.

• Applicants will receive answers: Ultimo March 2027.

• Fellowship begins: 1 September 2027.

About AIAS

As an 'Institute for Advanced Study,' AIAS brings researchers together across disciplines, seniority and nationality. AIAS offers fellowships for excellent researchers from all academic disciplines to pursue cutting-edge research projects for the benefit of society and humankind in optimal research conditions.

The daily encounter with colleagues from diverse research disciplines at AIAS provides fellows with fresh and different insights, methods and perspectives on their own research, leading to new and unexpected research questions and ideas.

Are you keen to support an organization that's on an exciting data journey? Then come join TDC Brands.

As the Data Governance Specialist, you will be a member of the Data Office, responsible for supporting and developing data governance initiatives across the organization. In this role you will work flexibly between the Data Office and embedded in business units to make data roles work day-to-day: enabling data consumers, assisting Data Domain Owners and Data Stewards.

You will have an important role in supporting data governance by working collaboratively with the business.

Key Responsibilities:

Enable Data Consumers:

• Support adoption of the strategic data platform and the Enterprise Business Glossary (EBG) among data consumers in your business domain, including AI and agentic consumers.

• Help consumers find, understand, and trust governed data so it actually gets used for business insights and automation.

Assist Data Domain Owners:

• Support your Data Domain Owner(s) in maturing the data domain map and semantic models.

• Align with Tech, DPO and Legal as needed when data domain priorities, critical data elements, or AI classifications are being set.

• Flag gaps early — missing owners, unclear sources, unresolved dependencies — so each wave starts on solid ground.

Assist Data Stewards:

Stakeholder Engagement and Communication:

• Act as the day-to-day point of contact for Data Domain Owners, Data Stewards, Glossary Term Owners and data consumers.

Bonus

Experience with telecoms, familiarity with data cataloging tools, or an interest in how governed data enables AI and agentic use cases.

Qualifications

As a Data Governance Specialist, we expect you to have sufficient years' experience in data management and data governance. You most likely come from an industry that prioritizes critical and valuable data assets and applies 'just enough' data governance.

Key expectations of the role are having great communication skills, comfort in operating pragmatically ahead of a fully defined policy landscape, and an ability to interact with people across the organization to produce tangible benefits to our data and AI initiatives.

Overview

Corti is the frontier lab for clinical-grade AI, building world-leading models and infrastructure for the realities of healthcare.

Our technology powers healthcare’s most ambitious software, from EHR vendors and virtual care platforms to the health systems that care depends on. We work with builders ranging from fast-moving startups to global healthcare enterprises, helping them bring clinical AI into real-world care.

Healthcare is full of problems where AI has to do more than simply work. Clinicians are overwhelmed by documentation. Coding errors, backlogs and denials cost health systems billions. And the specialist expertise patients need is not always available when they need it.

We build AI specifically for these environments, trained on real patient interactions, validated against real outcomes, and designed to perform where accuracy, trust and reliability matter. If you want to help define how AI is built for healthcare, you belong at Corti.

The Role

We’re looking for a GTM Engineer to help build the systems behind a smarter, more scalable go-to-market engine at Corti. You’ll connect the tools and data that power our commercial teams, turning fragmented systems into a reliable foundation for automation, insight, and action.

This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of software, data, and business impact. Data foundation

Own the event tracking layer, instrumenting key product and commercial touchpoints so analytics tools (PostHog, Mixpanel, etc.) reflect what's actually happening.

• 
Build enrichment pipelines that pull from third-party data providers and internal signals to keep ICP records current and scored.

Systems and automation

• 
Design and implement workflows, automations, and backend services that improve how commercial teams operate, from pipeline management and deal acceleration to post-sale handoffs.

• 
Identify repetitive GTM processes and systematically eliminate them through automation, freeing commercial teams to focus on higher-judgment work.

Activation and tooling

• 
Build systems that surface timely signals and enable proactive, data-driven GTM execution, including AI-powered internal tools and agentic workflows where appropriate.

• 
Build internal tools that reduce manual work for sales, CS, and growth, such as automated account research, meeting prep summaries, or usage-based alert systems.

• 
Partner with Growth and RevOps to define the data models and pipeline logic that underpin campaign targeting, segmentation, and attribution.

Cross-functional impact

• 
Collaborate as the primary technical builder for GTM teams across Growth, Enterprise Sales, Developer Experience, and Scaled Customer Experience, translating process needs into robust, scalable solutions.

• 
Document all built components so systems remain understandable and extensible as the team scales.

• 
Contribute to engineering quality through clean implementation, thoughtful code review, and cross-functional collaboration.

What you bring:

• 
Experience as a software engineer, ideally at mid-level, with exposure to growth, sales, or other go-to-market teams.

• 
Strong proficiency in Node.js and TypeScript, with a backend or server-side engineering focus.

• 
Experience integrating business-critical tools such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, or similar systems.

• 
Familiarity with analytics and data tooling such as PostHog, Mixpanel, Segment, Google Analytics, Amplitude, or Google Tag Manager.

• 
Experience working with ETL processes, data synchronization, or workflow automation is a plus, but not required.

• 
Excellent English verbal and written communication skills, including all-remote communication.

Life at Corti

You will be reporting to VP of Growth

• 
The position is full-time and starts as soon as possible.

• 
Hybrid working environment in Copenhagen

• 
Equipment provided by Corti

Ready to dive into the world of Corti? Hit that 'Apply' button, and let's start working together on reshaping the dialogue in healthcare, making a real difference for millions of patient outcomes around the world.

jobs.occupation: Senior Embedded Software Engineer, Real-Time Vision - Simulator Technology
jobs.description:
Shape the future of real-time vision in sports technology

Join Trackman’s new Simulator Technology team and help build next-generation camera systems for the world’s leading golf simulators. We are looking for an experienced engineer with expertise in real-time video pipelines, camera integration, and low-latency systems.

About the team

Trackman is the global leader in indoor golf technology, delivering advanced simulator experiences through precision tracking, virtual golf software, and in-bay technology.

Our new Simulator Technology´s (SimTech) mission is to drive innovation across the entire in-bay customer experience: cameras, projectors, kiosks, moving floors, and the software that ties them together. The team works in close collaboration with Trackman's hardware, tracking, ML, and Virtual Golf teams to deliver seamless, world-class experiences. This is a unique opportunity to become one of the first engineers shaping the future of Trackman’s simulator technology used by elite athletes and golfers around the world.

The role

You will help build a Windows-based real-time vision platform that captures camera streams, runs AI-based image analysis, and outputs video overlays. The role focuses on low-latency camera integration and high-performance video pipelines. This work sits at the heart of SimTech's camera platform the low-level foundation that everything from swing capture to AI coaching will be built on. Our current team is strong in vision/ML, and we need an engineer who specializes in camera integration and real-time video pipelines.

What you will do

• 
Design and implement low-latency camera capture pipelines on Windows.

• 
Integrate with 3rd party cameras using vendor SDKs as well as our own custom camera modules

• 
Build reliable frame pipelines from capture to inference handoff to overlay output.

• 
Optimize for stable FPS, low jitter, and deterministic end-to-end latency.

• 
Implement robust camera lifecycle handling: hot-plug, disconnect/reconnect, error recovery.

• 
Work closely with ML engineers to define frame formats, metadata, and timing contracts.

• 
Build diagnostics: dropped-frame counters, latency telemetry, and health logging.

• 
Support production readiness across different camera models and hardware configurations.

Success in this role means delivering stable, low-latency dual-camera pipelines with reliable recovery mechanisms, robust telemetry, and a well-documented architecture that enables the broader SimTech team to confidently build on the platform.

Job requirements

• 
5+ years in real-time video, machine vision, or camera systems engineering.

• 
Strong C++ (C++17 or newer) - preferably on Windows.

• 
Hands-on with Media Foundation and/or DirectShow capture stacks.

• 
Proven integration experience with industrial camera SDKs (IDS peak / uEye SDK strongly preferred).

• 
Deep understanding of pixel formats, color conversion, timestamps, and buffering.

• 
Solid grasp of USB3 Vision / GenICam concepts and camera controls (exposure, gain, trigger modes).

• 
Experience with multithreaded/parallel pipelines and performance profiling.

• 
Practical OpenCV experience for image handling and overlay operations.

• 
Experience designing fault-tolerant long-running services/applications.

Preferred qualifications: Experience with GStreamer or FFmpeg, GPU acceleration, multi-camera synchronization, inference runtimes, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and GenICam / USB3 Vision standards is considered a plus.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

Job description

Are you driven by designing robust software architecture and solving complex system-level challenges in high-performance, real-time environments? Do you want to build systems that turn raw sensor data into precise and real-time metrics that golfers and broadcasters rely on?

At Trackman, we combine radar technology, computer vision, and data intelligence to redefine how golf is played, practiced and experienced. From local golf clubs to live TV broadcasts, our products set the global standard for accuracy, performance, and innovation.

We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to play a central role in architecting and evolving the software systems behind Trackman Range and Golf Broadcast.

In this role, you will design and own key parts of our real-time data processing platform, ensuring it is scalable, maintainable, and performant under demanding conditions. You will work at the intersection of software engineering and applied algorithms, translating mathematical models and signal-processing concepts into robust, production-grade systems.

You will be responsible for system-level design decisions, improving software architecture, and driving engineering quality across the codebase. This includes diagnosing complex system behavior, addressing performance regressions, and ensuring high standards of reliability, testability, and maintainability.

Strong expertise in C++ and Python, with a track record of building high-performance, production-grade systems

•

Experience driving code quality, testing, CI/CD, and managing technical debt in production systems

• 
Experience with Linux-based systems for development, deployment, and debugging of distributed applications

• 
Experience with Docker for containerization and orchestration of those applications

• 
5+ years of relevant experience with ownership of critical systems or components

Computer vision, tracking, and camera calibration

• 
Real-time camera and video systems, including stream handling, data capture and encoding/decoding
